title: Component candidates — the register
note: THE DETECTOR the component bar was missing (the developer, 2026-09-02, PLAN batch 27 'go with recommendation'; filed by the lead as CC-1). components/CLAUDE.md sets the bar for a component — proven, owned, contracted — but nothing DETECTED a shared part before the third copy; brand-home x3 was caught by a manual survey. ONE ROW PER SHARED PART, on item `<slug>` ([a-z0-9-]): what it does · where it exists today (paths, and how many copies) · would-be consumers · the SIGNAL that raised it (carding = the lead filling a card's 'Shared parts:' line; design = a PLAN fold's 'Reuses / could be reused by' line; scanner = the CC-2 worker tick, reviewer mini-worker) · owner-if-extracted · DISPOSITION watch|extract|never. DISPOSITIONS ARE the developer'S — graduation stays his (INB-4); any seat may RAISE a row (open_items), a disposition record from anyone else is advisory and says so. THE RULE OF THREE (ruled with the kind): 1st use = a note on the card that builds it, never a row; 2nd use = a row here, disposition watch; 3rd use = an extraction card that BLOCKS the third copy. THE EXTRACTION BAR IS UNCHANGED: two real consumers + an owner + a contract; one consumer = a note, never a component — premature extraction freezes an untested contract. Records are an event history folded on read (serve_records history, the inbox pattern): a row is raised, then watched, then extracted or ruled never; the latest record's disposition is the current one. The reserved id `candidates-index` is the cumulative list of row ids and is how a browser enumerates rows (the platform lists records only per KNOWN item id — the inbox `filed-index` / tasks `task-index` / teardown `runs-index` mechanism); a seat that raises a row appends to it in the same act. KILL (on the whole system): three weeks on, if the register holds only scanner rows and none from carding, the human signal is dead — keep the scanner, drop the template line.

_reserved_ids.candidates-index: cumulative {ids: [...]} of every row raised, latest record wins; appended to by whoever raises a row, in the same act.

verdict_fields.note: exactly one per record. `index` appears only on `candidates-index`.
one line: what the shared part does (raise records)
list of repo paths where it exists today — the copies, each named (raise records)
integer, how many copies `where` lists (raise records)
list: builds or tools that use or would use it (raise records)
who would own the component; a name or 'unassigned' (raise records)
the developer's; on a raise record it is the proposal (always watch); on a disposition record it is the ruling when reviewer is the developer, advisory otherwise
